text:
My best friend passed away recently, and grieving before his grave I said,
"Bro, I really miss you. My wife has been pregnant for 8 months now. How about you reincarnate as my child?"
A month later, my wife gave birth to a big boy. As my child grew older each day, I realized he looks a lot like my best friend.
I'm really happy that my prayer worked.
gist: A man asks his dead best friend to reincarnate as his unborn son, and takes the boy's resemblance to the friend as proof the prayer worked, missing the affair.

characters.looks: naive happy man, flowers, black suit
pregnant woman, nervous sideways glance
boy who looks exactly like the dead friend
best friend in photo on gravestone, distinctive mustache

text:
Jack wakes up with a horrible hangover and a throbbing black eye.
The first thing he sees is a single rose on the side table and a note from his wife: “Dear, breakfast is made. I’ve gone shopping to make you your favorite dinner tonight. I love you!”
He stumbles to the kitchen and, sure enough, there’s breakfast. “Joe,” he says to his son, “what happened last night?”
“You came home soused and got that black eye tripping over a chair.”
“So, why the rose, breakfast, and sweet note from your mother?”
“Oh, that. Mom dragged you to the bedroom, and when she tried to take off your clothes, you screamed, ‘Leave me alone, I’m married!’”
gist: A hungover husband finds a loving note and breakfast from his wife, and his son explains that drunk, he fought off her undressing him shouting he was married.

characters.looks: hungover man, black eye, messy hair, rumpled shirt
teenage son eating cereal, amused smirk
smiling woman, shopping bags

text:
I was browsing in a liquor store when an employee asked me “Do you need help?”
I said, “Yes, but I’m here to get whiskey instead.”
gist: A liquor store clerk asks if he needs help and he says yes, but he's here for whiskey instead, taking help as psychological help.

wordplay.explanation: 'Do you need help' as shop assistance vs needing help for a drinking problem.

characters.looks: disheveled man, tired eyes, basket of bottles
friendly store clerk, name tag, vest

text:
Two boys are arguing when the teacher enters the classroom. The teacher says, “What are you two arguing about?”
One boy answers, “We found a ten-dollar bill and decided whoever tells the biggest lie gets to keep it.”
“You two should be ashamed of yourselves,” said the teacher. “When I was your age, I didn’t even know what a lie was.”
The boys looked at each other and handed the ten dollars to the teacher.
gist: Boys hold a lying contest for found money; the teacher scolds them, claiming she never knew what a lie was at their age, and they hand her the prize for the biggest lie.

characters.looks: schoolboy, messy hair, backpack, sly grin
schoolboy, freckles, holding ten-dollar bill
prim teacher, glasses, cardigan, pointing finger

Question after question..."who's blood is it?"....."where did you get it?"....."why is it in a bucket?
